# How to Create a Marketing Video with AI Tools in 30 Minutes

Thirty minutes is honest for a simple marketing video — a product clip, an event promo, a testimonial-style piece — provided you accept what AI can and cannot do in that window. AI excels at the assembly line: script, voiceover, stock visuals, captions, music. It cannot replace the two decisions that actually make a marketing video work: the hook and the call to action. So this workflow handles everything else in half-hour blocks, with honest tool picks for each step.

## Step 1: Script and hook (8 minutes)

Start with [[link:/tools/6|ChatGPT]] (Freemium): give it your product, audience, and one-sentence value prop, and ask for a 30-second script with the hook in the first three seconds. Drafts need a human edit — ChatGPT's answers can contain confident-sounding errors, and marketing claims need fact-checking. [[link:/tools/561|Video Script AI]] (Freemium) is a more focused alternative for script drafting and idea outlining, though drafts still need editing to match brand voice.

## Step 2: Voiceover (5 minutes)

[[link:/tools/78|Murf AI]] (Freemium) turns the script into narration for corporate videos and e-learning. The free plan is limited to 10 minutes of voice generation, which covers this use case but not a content series. [[link:/tools/468|Play.ht]] (Freemium) is an alternative for expressive, natural-sounding narration — the free tier caps length and voice choices. Pick one voice and keep it consistent across your videos; consistency is what makes a series feel like a brand.

## Step 3: Visuals (8 minutes)

[[link:/tools/201|Pictory]] (Freemium) converts your script or blog post into video with stock footage — blog-to-video content and highlight clips are its core use. Remember its limits: output is capped at 1080p, and editing capabilities are limited compared with dedicated editors. [[link:/tools/279|InVideo]] (Freemium) is the template route: marketing videos and social clips from templates, though free exports typically include watermarks and limited resolution.

## Step 4: Edit, captions, music (7 minutes)

Assemble in [[link:/tools/51|VEED.io]] (Freemium): add captions — most viewers watch muted — trim pacing, and layer a music bed. [[link:/tools/1512|CapCut]] (Freemium) does the same job with auto captions and one-click polish, and is closer to how social-native editors think. For the music, [[link:/tools/69|Soundraw]] (Freemium) generates instrumental beds quickly, and its instrumental focus suits background use.

## Step 5: Export and check (2 minutes)

Export vertical and horizontal versions if you are posting to multiple platforms, watch it once muted to confirm the captions carry the message, and verify any factual claims in the script one last time.

## What AI cannot do in 30 minutes

The hook. The targeting. The decision about whether this video should exist at all. Those are yours, and they determine whether the assembly-line output actually converts.

## Common mistakes

Letting AI write the hook — it rarely lands; shipping a video without captions; exceeding free-tier minutes mid-series; and producing five clips that all sound the same.

## FAQ

**Is 30 minutes realistic?** Yes for simple clips, if the hook and CTA are pre-decided.

**Which voice tool?** Murf AI free covers a 10-minute video; longer needs a paid plan.

**Do I need stock footage?** Pictory and InVideo include it; licensing is bundled.

**What if I need 4K?** Pictory caps at 1080p; VEED's browser editing handles longer projects better.

**Can I reuse the workflow weekly?** Yes — save the script prompt, voice, and music bed as templates.

**What if my footage is messy?** [[link:/tools/1535|Adobe Podcast AI]] (Freemium) cleans audio; [[link:/tools/51|VEED.io]] (Freemium) fixes visual pacing.

## Pricing at a glance

The 30-minute workflow runs entirely on free tiers: ChatGPT, Murf AI's 10-minute free voice allowance, Pictory's free video length, VEED or CapCut free editing, and Soundraw's free music generation. The caps that matter are Murf's 10 minutes and Pictory's video length limits — both fine for a single marketing clip, both felt immediately if you try to run a weekly series on free plans. The first paid upgrade most creators make is the voice tool, because a consistent voice across videos is what makes a series feel like a brand.

## Where the 30 minutes actually goes

Script: 8. Voiceover: 5. Visuals: 8. Edit and captions: 7. Export and check: 2. Notice what is missing: filming. This workflow assumes stock or generated visuals plus a voice track, which is the honest trade of AI video — you skip the camera, the crew, and the location, and you accept a slightly more generic visual register. For product explainers and event promos that trade is usually correct; for anything where the product must be seen, film the footage yourself and use AI only for the assembly steps.
tldr: Thirty minutes works for simple marketing videos if you pre-decide the hook: script with ChatGPT, voice with Murf, visuals with Pictory, finish in VEED or CapCut with captions.
